name: Jawbox
label: Dischord
lede: Jawbox sent Atlantic a list of demands and Atlantic said yes to every line. The band got a song on Beavis and Butt-Head, and hate mail from D.C.

eras.title: A sink, a sewer, a television
eras.text: J. Robbins had been playing bass in Government Issue; now he wanted his own band, on guitar and vocals. With Kim Coletta on bass and Adam Wade on drums, Jawbox came up fast in a D.C. scene trading hardcore speed for something knottier.

years.h: Brewer's Dictionary supplies the name: a sink, a sewer, or the TV
years.p: [[J. Robbins|3babd931-a940-43a8-b629-d7aed5b821d9]], [[Kim Coletta|f220e94d-883b-46ce-a459-9463cce7f55d]] and [[Adam Wade|d2502278-bf42-445b-98a2-9249af4c8a0a]] find "jawbox" in Brewer's Dictionary of Phrase and Fable, which lists it as all three.

years.h: Jawbox debut in September 1989, opening for Fugazi and Shudder to Think
years.p: A self-titled demo EP circulates the same year, and Bullet Park ends up on a Maximumrocknroll compilation.
years.xp: Dischord's band page says only that Jawbox opened for [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] in 1989. Wikipedia supplies the month and puts [[Shudder to Think|5a6e19e0-3ff0-4b3d-869e-3c539d6d8707]] on the same bill.

years.h: Kim Coletta's DeSoto label debuts with Tools & Chrome
years.p: Jawbox's first single is a joint release from Dischord and DeSoto, the label Coletta runs. DeSoto issues the band's vinyl from then on.

eras.title: A second guitar, then a new drummer
eras.text: Jawbox's Dischord years were short and loud. Bill Barbot joined as second guitarist, Chicago engineer Iain Burgess gave them a heavier sound on Novelty, and by the end of 1992 Wade was gone.

years.cap: Jawbox at the Euclid Tavern, Cleveland, 1991
years.h: Grippe costs under $2,000 and becomes Dischord No. 52
years.p: [[Eli Janney|d727e531-da9c-4124-ac66-0f79fb884d45]] produces the debut album. Grip is the one song from it the band keeps playing.
years.xp:
Robbins told Louder you can hear "we're a very young band" on Grippe.

It sold well for a first record: Wikipedia ranks Jawbox as Dischord's third best-selling band, behind [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] and Fugazi.

years.h: Drummer Adam Wade's roommate becomes Jawbox's second guitarist
years.p: [[Bill Barbot|c0407a04-3b21-4274-9ed1-695fbc07b218]] joins on guitar and vocals around the Grippe release. 1991 also brings a split single with [[Jawbreaker|ec88cdc3-0517-4951-b5ef-7323e7316db0]] and a tour with [[Helmet|582fee78-d934-4603-9f5c-1729e0ca36b7]].

years.h: The Tongues single fills the gap, Dischord No. 61
years.p: It arrives in early 1992, between Grippe and Novelty.

q: Jawbox sold like 40,000. The next step up really is Minor Threat and Fugazi.
years.h: Novelty is recorded in five days by the engineer behind Big Black
years.p: Dischord No. 69. [[Iain Burgess|1572ff4f-9714-4d7e-804a-49b86a74a855]], who also engineered [[Big Black|9463868f-edc8-427e-ac07-ea89698e5f15]] and [[Naked Raygun|85d2e30c-92fd-4c7f-a2dc-f988a70e234d]], sleeps on Robbins' couch in Chicago during the sessions.
years.xp:
Robbins told Louder Burgess "managed to bring his aesthetic to that record without ever being a svengali about it." He also said the sound really expanded with Barbot in the band. Static and Cutoff are his favorites; Cutoff got the video.

[[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]], sizing up the Dischord catalog, put Jawbox just below the label's two biggest bands.

years.cap: Jawbox at the Euclid Tavern, Cleveland
years.h: Wade walks out after the Novelty tour
years.p: Adam Wade leaves as soon as the tour ends and soon joins [[Shudder to Think|5a6e19e0-3ff0-4b3d-869e-3c539d6d8707]]. [[Zach Barocas|0c8ab49f-f5d0-46b5-bee5-5aa496a70ece]], a friend already living in the band's building, takes the drums.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia, Wade had grown frustrated with what was going on inside Jawbox before and during the tour: Robbins and Coletta had ended their relationship, Coletta and Barbot had become a couple, and Robbins' behavior turned erratic.

Robbins said Barocas' arrival really changed the band.

eras.title: Atlantic says yes to everything
eras.text: Grunge had major labels shopping in punk basements, and Jawbox had offers from Epic, Mercury and Atlantic. They signed with Atlantic and left Dischord, and kept a surprising amount of control. D.C. treated it as a betrayal anyway.

years.h: Motorist / Jackpot Plus! is the last Dischord single
years.p: Dischord No. 77, two songs out in 1993 before Jawbox sign to Atlantic and start For Your Own Special Sweetheart.

years.big: "We would be stupid not to do it."
years.h: Jawbox go to Atlantic, demands intact
years.p: J. Robbins on the offer. The band's list asked for self-management, full creative control and vinyl on DeSoto, and Atlantic agreed to all of it.
years.xp:
The list also covered the recording budget, merchandising and European licensing. Jawbox turned down a big advance and tour support, asking only for studio money and enough to settle old bills. [[Mike Gitter|942763ba-3882-48b4-b0a4-513f53849530]], who knew them from the Boston hardcore scene, was their A&R man.

D.C. took it badly. One letter-writer, the band later recalled, hoped they'd die in a fiery van accident. Barocas said the deal kept Jawbox together: he had already quit and applied to the University of Maryland.

years.cap: J. Robbins at the Hardback Cafe, Gainesville
years.h: Seven weeks in the studio, against the usual seven days
years.p: [[Ted Niceley|fbe203ef-a327-4d7e-af16-a10d55b7347d]], who made the early [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] records, produces the Atlantic debut. It peaks at No. 28 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart and, per Wikipedia, sells about 50,000.
years.xp: Louder notes the usual Jawbox budget was a week. The band's Atlantic terms put it on DeSoto vinyl, with Barocas on drums for the first time on a full album.

years.h: Savory makes MTV, Conan and Beavis and Butt-Head
years.p: 120 Minutes puts the single in rotation and hosts Jawbox in the studio; Late Night with Conan O'Brien books them too. The follow-up, Cooling Card, barely registers.

years.h: Jawbox go out as Stone Temple Pilots' opening act
years.p: A year after leaving Dischord, they take a support slot on a 1994 Stone Temple Pilots tour.

years.h: Live at Lee's Palace, Toronto, August 19, 1994
yt: Live at Lee's Palace, Toronto, August 19, 1994

eras.title: The best record, on a label about to fold
eras.text: Jawbox made Jawbox, the album Robbins still calls their best, then watched TAG, the Atlantic imprint releasing it, disappear. By 1997 drummer Zach Barocas was headed for film school and the band was done.

years.h: Leatherface and Jawbox share a live LP in Germany
years.p: It's part of the Your Choice Live Series. Jawbox also record sessions for John Peel that year.

yt: Full set at the HFStival, RFK Stadium, 1996
years.h: The hometown band goes on first at the HFStival
years.p: At RFK Stadium, the D.C. radio festival gives Jawbox the day's earliest slot. A VHS recording of the whole set is online.

years.h: Jawbox arrives on a label about to fold
years.p: Produced by [[John Agnello|c7d979e9-3b10-43db-973b-7da55a8a33c7]] and out on TAG, a new Atlantic imprint. Robbins calls it "our best record."
years.xp:
Agnello had worked with [[Dinosaur Jr.|77c167d2-4965-4421-830a-9815e4956475]] and [[Chavez|c08d2dcd-3c9a-4e5c-b444-c48936de2707]]. A cover of [[Tori Amos|c0b2500e-0cef-4130-869d-732b23ed9df5]]' Cornflake Girl hides at the end. Desert Sea, Robbins' favorite, came out of a jam, and Mirrorful was the single.

Wikipedia puts sales near 40,000. Robbins said the record fizzled along with the label, and in early 1997 Jawbox and Atlantic agreed to part.

years.cap: Jawbox at the Hardback Cafe, Gainesville, with Barocas out of frame
years.h: Barocas leaves for film school, and Europe is cancelled
years.p: Zach Barocas heads to Hunter College in New York. [[Peter Moffett|09d1a7e7-51fd-4b48-b99b-5b6bcbc8865b]], ex-[[Government Issue|9b952ee8-d45d-4a26-8066-57849d871e06]], takes the drums, but the planned European tour is scrapped.
years.xp:
It wasn't the first time Barocas had walked. He had already quit once and applied to the University of Maryland, and said the Atlantic deal was what kept Jawbox going.

Moffett, who had also drummed in Wool, stayed on with Robbins and Barbot in [[Burning Airlines|5ea472eb-5040-410c-b021-1e678276aed9]].

years.cap: Kim Coletta and J. Robbins at the Black Cat, Washington, January 24, 1997
years.h: Jawbox end it with Atlantic out of the picture
years.p: With the label deal over and Moffett on drums, Jawbox formally break up in 1997.

years.h: Coletta and Barbot, bass and guitar, get married
years.p: With Jawbox finished, the two marry later in 1997, Wikipedia reports.
years.xp: They had a son in 2001. According to Wikipedia they divorced shortly after 2009. Both were back on stage together for the 2019 reunion, and Coletta kept running DeSoto.

eras.title: Scrapbooks and airplanes
eras.text: Jawbox's odds and ends got collected on My Scrapbook of Fatal Accidents, and Robbins and Barbot went straight into Burning Airlines with Jawbox's last drummer, Peter Moffett. Robbins was also becoming one of the busiest producers in post-hardcore.

years.h: My Scrapbook of Fatal Accidents sweeps up the leftovers
years.p: B-sides, outtakes, Peel Sessions, live tracks and covers, gathered on Coletta's DeSoto label.

years.cap: J. Robbins at the Black Cat, Washington, D.C.
years.h: Robbins starts Burning Airlines, and keeps producing
years.p: He, Barbot and Moffett start releasing records on DeSoto as [[Burning Airlines|5ea472eb-5040-410c-b021-1e678276aed9]].
years.xp: Robbins' producer credits pile up in these years: [[Texas Is the Reason|b93c736f-a82f-4cae-9e57-a60b12d7055f]], [[Jets to Brazil|675ec992-a8e4-41f8-b28b-1aad0c8a9ad1]], [[Shiner|85e4c862-bafe-48a2-a7af-b87cc3d8a7f3]], later [[Against Me!|a66ebddc-ff04-46b8-820a-15c63e80dba1]] and [[Clutch|0cdb0359-5698-487d-9aae-a25fb4dcdc4d]].

years.h: September 11 derails Burning Airlines
years.p: The band of Robbins, Barbot and Moffett splits in 2002 after the aftermath of the attacks wrecks their touring.

eras.title: One song on network TV
eras.text: Twelve years after the split, For Your Own Special Sweetheart came back into print on the band's own terms, and Jawbox played exactly one TV spot to celebrate.

years.h: Sweetheart returns, remastered by Bob Weston
years.p: DeSoto and Dischord reissue the Atlantic debut on CD and LP with new artwork.

years.h: One song on Late Night, and Robbins says that's it
years.p: Jawbox play Savory on Late Night with Jimmy Fallon, their first performance since 1997. Robbins calls it their only show.
years.xp:
The occasion was the reissue of For Your Own Special Sweetheart. Savory went out on the broadcast; 68 and FF=66 were posted online.

The next Jawbox show was almost ten years away.

eras.title: Back on the road, then done again
eras.text: This time it was a real reunion: tours, a live album, new recordings. It ran six years, swapped Barbot for Harlan on guitar, and ended with Robbins confirming in a newsletter that Jawbox was done.

years.cap: Kim Coletta and Zach Barocas at the 9:30 Club, Washington, June 2019
years.h: Jawbox book a summer tour, their first in more than twenty years
years.p: Twelve dates with Robbins, Coletta, Barbot and Barocas. The Metro in Chicago becomes Live at Metro Chicago 2019 on Arctic Rodeo.

years.h: Barbot's commute from Vermont opens a guitar slot for Brooks Harlan
years.p: Barbot leaves in August 2021. [[Brooks Harlan|f9cb849f-568b-4987-b9cc-96e0e5d7d790]], of [[War on Women|69c05e9a-883b-4570-9c3d-c4bfc896a488]] and a longtime Robbins collaborator, takes his place.

years.h: The Revisionist EP is the first new Jawbox in 26 years
years.p: Jawbox self-release it first, then Arctic Rodeo puts it out, the label behind Live at Metro Chicago 2019.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists re-recordings of Grippe songs and a Wire cover among the tracks. It is Harlan's recorded debut with the band.

years.h: Robbins tells a newsletter Jawbox is done for the foreseeable future
years.p: Las Vegas, October 12, 2024, at Best Friends Forever, was the last show. Robbins said so in April 2025 to Kyle Ryan's Band Name Bureau.
